ai.title: Agentic system personalizes physical controls to help users “DJ their art”
ai.brief: In 2017, Apple removed the home button from its iPhones. Users lost a convenient, tangible control — part of a larger shift to digital buttons, knobs, and sliders we also see in cars (like with radio presets and air conditioning) and kitchens (see smart fridges). We can’t leave physical controls behind entirely, though. They tend to be more convenient and efficient — think of how you can use a physical gaming controller without looking at it — and, at times, more precise, like when you use a dial to get the volume just right. But tangible controls are typically preprogrammed to do a specific thing, minimizing their usefulness.

This vulnerability affects the VMware Directory Service (vmdir) in vCenter. An attacker with network access to a vulnerable server could exploit the flaw to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access. Broadcom published the issue in its security advisory VMSA-2026-0011 . The company credited researchers from Qianxin, depthfirst, and ThreatBook for independently reporting the vulnerability.
